title: Software Patent Infringement: How to Build a Defensible Read
summary: Learn how to analyze software patent infringement under U.S. law, from claim construction and evidence to SaaS actors, source code, and remedies.
body_markdown:
Software patent disputes rarely turn on whether two products seem similar. They turn on the language of a particular claim, the operation of a particular software version, and the acts of particular parties.


That makes a disciplined infringement read valuable long before suit. Patent owners can focus on claims and products with complete evidence. Accused companies can identify a missing limitation, a claim-construction dispute, or a divided-infringement issue before costs compound. U.S. utility patent law supplies the framework here.


## Key takeaways


- Literal infringement requires every limitation of at least one asserted claim. A strong match on five limitations cannot make up for a missing sixth.
- Copying is unnecessary. Independently written code can infringe a patent, while copied code may raise copyright issues without meeting a patent claim.
- Claim type controls the proof. For direct infringement of a method claim, every step must be performed by or attributable to a single entity. A system or computer-readable-storage-medium claim may turn on the product's capabilities and configuration.
- Software evidence needs a version, date, configuration, actor, and location. A generic product name is rarely a complete accused instrumentality.
- Source code can resolve hidden implementation questions, but public documentation, testing, logs, and architecture evidence often establish the foundation first.

It maps evidence to claim limitations and moves supported findings into an evidence-of-use chart. Our guide to[AI infringement detection](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/ai-patent-infringement-detection) explains the portfolio-scale workflow. ## What is software patent infringement?


Software patent infringement occurs when an unauthorized party commits an act covered by[35 U.S.C. § 271](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/35/271) , such as making, using, selling, offering to sell, or importing an invention that falls within a patent claim. For literal infringement, the accused software or its use must satisfy every limitation of at least one claim.


Patent claims protect the claimed invention. Copyright protects original expression, including source code. Patent infringement therefore does not require access to the patent owner's code or proof of copying. The accused team may have built its product independently and still practice the claim.


Patent eligibility and validity are separate questions. A software claim may be challenged under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, or 112, and each issued claim is[presumed valid](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/35/282) unless that presumption is overcome. An infringement analysis should track invalidity defenses in parallel rather than treat them as substitutes for the claim comparison.


### The main infringement theories


Theory What must be shown Software example


Literal direct infringement For an applicable § 271(a) act, an accused apparatus or system meets every limitation. Every method step is performed by or attributable to a single entity A SaaS provider performs some steps itself and directs or controls customer performance of the remaining steps


Doctrine of equivalents An accused feature that falls outside the literal language is equivalent on a limitation-by-limitation basis A different data structure performs substantially the same function, in substantially the same way, to obtain substantially the same result, subject to legal limits on equivalents


Induced infringement A third party directly infringes; the accused inducer knows the induced acts constitute infringement and takes active steps to encourage them Documentation directs customers to enable and use a feature in an infringing workflow


Contributory infringement Another party directly infringes; the accused contributor supplies a material component specially made or adapted for infringement, with the required knowledge, and the component lacks a substantial noninfringing use A software module is distributed for use in a patented system and has no substantial noninfringing use


The doctrine of equivalents cannot erase a claim limitation or compare products only at a high level. *Warner-Jenkinson* requires the analysis to preserve the role of[each individual element](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/520/17) .


Inducement also requires more than a foreseeable customer use. In 2026, the Supreme Court held in *Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. v. Amarin Pharma, Inc.* that ordinary acts incident to product distribution, knowledge of infringing potential or actual use, omissions or inaction, and vague statements combined with speculation are insufficient. The pleaded facts must support affirmative conduct designed to encourage infringement. The[unanimous decision](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/25pdf/24-889_5i36.pdf) gives software teams a current reason to examine setup guides, feature prompts, training, support scripts, and marketing language alongside the technical read.


Willfulness is different. It is a potential basis for enhanced damages after infringement, not an additional way to prove infringement.


## How to analyze software patent infringement


### 1. Select the claims and confirm the legal record


Start with the patent's current record. Confirm ownership, term, maintenance status, terminal disclaimers, reexamination or post-grant certificates, prosecution history, and any licenses that may reach the accused activity. These facts affect standing, scope, defenses, and remedies even though they are not substitutes for proving infringement.


Choose the independent and dependent claims that fit the accused architecture. A narrower dependent claim may produce the cleaner read when its added limitation matches a documented feature. Record the alleged infringement period because the product, claim scope, and available damages may change over time.


### 2. Construe the claim before mapping the product


Claim construction defines the comparison. Begin with the claim language, then read the specification and prosecution history as one intrinsic record. Identify express definitions, disclaimers, amendments, and arguments used to distinguish prior art. Extrinsic material such as dictionaries and expert testimony can help, but it should not rewrite the public record.


Terms such as “real time,” “client,” “automatically,” “configured to,” and “in response to” often determine a software case. Functional limitations and limitations governed by 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) may require close attention to the disclosed structure or algorithm. The Supreme Court's *Markman* decision assigns claim construction to the judge, which is why an early construction position should be explicit and source-grounded.[Read the decision](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/USREPORTS-517/USREPORTS-517-370) .


Maintain a construction log beside the claim chart. For each disputed term, state the proposed construction, supporting intrinsic evidence, competing construction, and effect on the read. That keeps a promising product match from silently depending on an untested definition.


### 3. Define the accused instrumentality precisely


**Synthetic teaching example: Every matter-specific name, identifier, patent identifier, software or version label, document title, source citation, product feature, configuration, date, and finding in the identification and chart below is invented. The linked statutes and judicial decisions elsewhere on this page are real legal authorities.**


A useful synthetic identification looks like “SYNTH-SOFTWARE-01, SYNTH-RELEASE-8.4, SYNTH-CONFIG-ENTERPRISE-A, SYNTH-FEATURE-ANOMALY enabled, deployed in SYNTH-REGION-US-01 during SYNTH-PERIOD-01.” “SYNTH-SOFTWARE-01” alone leaves too many factual gaps.


Capture at least:


- product and module names;
- release, build, or commit identifiers;
- paid tier, license key, and feature flags;
- default and optional configurations;
- client, server, cloud region, and third-party components;
- dates when the relevant behavior existed;
- the actor that performs or triggers each function.


This discipline prevents evidence from one release or configuration from being used to fill a limitation in another.


### 4. Build an evidence-of-use chart


Once the accused product and release are fixed, divide the claim into discrete limitations and map each limitation to the best available source. Lead with the technical mapping, place the pinpoint citation immediately before the cited excerpt or screenshot, and state any gap in the same evidence cell. The synthetic example below applies a literal-infringement theory.


Claim limitation Evidence


Receive encrypted telemetry from a client device SYNTH-FEATURE-TELEMETRY maps the encrypted client transmission because the API description identifies the source, destination, and transport. See page 1: “SYNTH-FEATURE-TELEMETRY transmits client-device payloads to the SYNTH-INGEST endpoint over TLS 1.3.” SYNTH-CAPTURE-01 maps receipt by the identified endpoint in SYNTH-CONFIG-ENTERPRISE-A. See page 1: Together, these synthetic sources support the limitation for the identified configuration.


Store each payload in a partition selected using a customer identifier SYNTH-DOC-ARCH-01 partially maps the storage limitation because it describes tenant separation without identifying the input used to select a partition. See page 3: The excerpt does not show that SYNTH-FEATURE-PARTITION uses a customer identifier to select the partition. Construction and implementation evidence remain necessary.


Apply a trained anomaly model to the stored payload SYNTH-DOC-ADMIN-01 fails to map the trained-model limitation because it describes static threshold logic instead. See page 5: No cited source identifies SYNTH-FEATURE-MODEL or shows a trained model operating on a stored payload. The limitation is unsupported on the synthetic record.


Generate an alert when an anomaly score exceeds a threshold SYNTH-DOC-USER-01 maps the documented relationship between the score, threshold, and resulting alert. See page 7: “SYNTH-FEATURE-ALERT creates an alert when the anomaly score exceeds the configured value.” SYNTH-LOG-01 maps the same sequence in SYNTH-CONFIG-ENTERPRISE-A. See page 1: The documentation and event record support this limitation for the identified configuration.


The record still does not establish literal infringement. The trained-model limitation has no supporting evidence, and the partition-selection limitation remains incomplete. Strong support elsewhere cannot cure either gap. The next investigation should target SYNTH-FEATURE-MODEL and SYNTH-FEATURE-PARTITION rather than add cumulative material to supported rows. A final chart should follow the same source discipline as[submission-ready claim charts](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/submission-ready-claim-charts-with-ai) .


### 5. Match the theory to the claim type, actor, and territory


For direct infringement of a method claim, every step must be performed by or attributable to a single entity. When several actors participate, the Federal Circuit's en banc *Akamai v. Limelight* opinion recognizes attribution where one entity directs or controls another's performance or where the actors form a joint enterprise. Direction or control can exist when an alleged infringer conditions participation in an activity or receipt of a benefit on performance of claimed steps and establishes the manner or timing of that performance. The inquiry is factual, and supplying software or general technical support does not by itself resolve it.[Read the official opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/9-1372.opinion.8-11-2015.1.pdf) .


System claims ask a different “use” question. A party may use a distributed system by putting the whole system into service and obtaining its benefit without physically possessing every server. *Centillion Data Systems v. Qwest* applied that rule to customer queries that triggered back-end processing.[The opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/10-1110-1131.pdf) shows why system use depends on control and benefit across the complete claimed system.


The Federal Circuit's 2024 *CloudofChange v. NCR* decision is a contrasting system-claim example. The claims required vendor-hosted server software and subscriber-controlled point-of-sale components. Merchants put the full system into service and received its benefit, so they were the users. NCR supplied only part of the system and did not direct or control the merchants' decision to subscribe, download the app, and use the complete system. The court therefore declined to attribute the merchants' system use to NCR.[Read the court's analysis](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1111.OPINION.12-18-2024_2438003.pdf) .


Territory matters as well. Section 271(a) reaches specified acts within the United States and imports into the United States. Record the location of servers, users, testing, sales, and each claimed method step rather than treating a globally distributed service as a single place.


### 6. Run noninfringement and invalidity in parallel


The strongest analysis tries to disprove its own first read. For every limitation, document the best noninfringement position. Evaluate claim construction, absent steps, optional modes, divided performance, license or exhaustion, and territorial gaps. Separately map prior art and other validity challenges to the asserted claims.


This two-track work changes decisions. A patent owner may find a cleaner claim or accused version. An accused company may find that a design change removes one limitation while preserving product value. Both sides get a clearer view of discovery needs, settlement posture, and litigation risk.


## What evidence proves how software works?


Use the least intrusive source that reliably proves the limitation, then move deeper where the record remains incomplete.


Evidence source Best use Common limitation


Product pages, manuals, datasheets, and API documentation Establish advertised features, inputs, outputs, supported configurations, and instructions May simplify behavior or omit internal implementation


Archived pages, release notes, package manifests, and repositories Tie a feature to a date and version Public history may be incomplete


Screenshots, videos, and instrumented product testing Show visible behavior and reproduce a workflow; preserve timestamps and test conditions for[video infringement evidence](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/video-as-prior-art-and-infringement-evidence) Output may support several possible internal mechanisms


Network traces, logs, database records, and configuration files Connect events, actors, timing, data flows, and enabled modes Collection conditions and provenance must be preserved


Architecture documents, tickets, and technical testimony Explain design decisions and component relationships Descriptions must be tied to the accused release


Binaries, decompilation, and source code Resolve hidden logic, control flow, data structures, and feature gates Code still must be connected to the shipped or deployed build and actual accused conduct


Source code is evidence, not a universal prerequisite. In *Finjan v. Secure Computing* , the Federal Circuit upheld infringement of system and storage-medium claims where the accused products contained locked code written to perform the claimed functions. The claim language covered capability. The same court reversed the method-claim verdict because the evidence showed only one test in Germany and no performance of every claimed step in the United States.[Finjan's claim-specific result](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/09-1576.pdf) is a useful check against treating “the code is present” as a complete answer.


Discovery requests should therefore identify the unresolved limitation, relevant module, product version, and expected code path. The Northern District of California's[Patent Local Rules](https://cand.uscourts.gov/rules-forms-fees/local-rules/patent-local-rules) pair specific infringement contentions with production of source code or other technical documents sufficient to show the operation of accused aspects. That sequence rewards a focused public-evidence chart before a broad code review.


## What should each side do first?


Patent owner or prospective plaintiff Accused company


Preserve the patent family, assignment chain, prosecution history, claim constructions, and licensing record With counsel, assess whether litigation is reasonably anticipated; if so, issue an appropriately scoped preservation notice covering relevant releases and evidence.


Chart the strongest claim against a named product version and configuration Rebuild the chart from the accused side and identify the first unsupported limitation under each reasonable construction


Capture dated public evidence with full URLs, files, metadata, screenshots, and test conditions Separate standard features from custom code, third-party components, optional modes, and customer-controlled steps


Identify which limitations require confidential discovery and why Analyze license, exhaustion, territory, prior use, invalidity, and unenforceability defenses separately


Assess marking, actual notice, sales, and the available damages period Evaluate a version-specific design-around and preserve evidence of when it ships


Keep literal, equivalents, induced, and contributory theories in separate rows Review customer instructions and support material for active encouragement of the accused use


A claim chart should remain a living record. Update it when claim construction changes, a new release ships, discovery reveals a different code path, or testing disproves an assumption.


## Remedies and exposure


Under[35 U.S.C. § 284](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/35/284) , compensatory damages cannot be less than a reasonable royalty, and a court may increase damages up to three times the assessed amount. Lost profits may be available when the evidence supports them. Enhanced damages are discretionary and reserved for culpable conduct under *Halo Electronics v. Pulse Electronics* , rather than following automatically from awareness of a patent.[Read Halo](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/USREPORTS-579/USREPORTS-579-93) .


Injunctions are also case-specific. A patent owner must satisfy the[traditional equitable test](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/USREPORTS-547/USREPORTS-547-388) ; infringement alone does not make a permanent injunction automatic. For patents covering articles made or sold by the patentee, compliance with[35 U.S.C. § 287](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/35/287) marking or proof of actual notice can control when damages begin.[35 U.S.C. § 286](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/35/286) generally bars recovery for infringement more than six years before the complaint or counterclaim.


## Frequently asked questions


### Are software patents enforceable in the United States?


Yes. There is no categorical rule making software patents unenforceable. Particular claims may still fail because they cover ineligible subject matter, are invalid, are unenforceable, or do not read on the accused software. The answer comes from the issued claim, its legal record, and the accused facts.


### Does reading a patent automatically create treble-damages liability?


No. Knowledge can matter to willfulness and indirect infringement, but awareness alone does not automatically produce enhanced damages. Section 284 gives the court discretion to increase damages after infringement, and *Halo* reserves enhancement for culpable conduct.[35 U.S.C. § 298](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?edition=prelim&num=0&req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title35-section298) also says that failure to obtain or present an opinion of counsel cannot be used to prove willfulness or intent to induce.


### Can open-source software infringe a patent?


Yes. Public source code and independent development do not create immunity from patent claims. A project or downstream user may have an express patent license, an implied license, exhaustion rights, or another defense, depending on the license and distribution chain. Those questions should be analyzed separately from whether the software practices every claim limitation.


### Can a design-around avoid software patent infringement?


Yes, when the revised product omits or materially changes at least one required limitation and does not infringe under the doctrine of equivalents. The design-around analysis should cover dependent claims, alternative configurations, customer workflows, and the exact release that reaches the market.
